sections.title: Getting started
sections.summary: New here? The Set up guide walks you through it (macOS is automatic; Windows needs a one-time loopMIDI setup). After that: connect the controller and start Live. The script starts the Maschine Bridge, which takes over the hardware: no Controller Editor, no MIDI mode, a real SHIFT key. While Live loads, the screen shows Waiting for Live; when the set is ready, a rainbow wave sweeps across the pads. Your note repeat rate, arp settings, chord type and voicing, drum colours and velocity curve are remembered between Live sessions.

tour.intro: Connect the controller and start Live: the Maschine Bridge takes over the hardware, with a real SHIFT key. No Controller Editor, no MIDI mode.

notes.title: Using the MASCHINE plug-in (Expansions)
notes.text: NI's MASCHINE plug-in (VST / AU) takes the controller as soon as it is anywhere in the set, and keeps it until it is deleted: selecting another track or switching the plug-in off doesn't release it. Meanwhile the script steps aside: the lights, screen and pads are MASCHINE's, and Live's status bar says so. Delete the last MASCHINE plug-in and the controller is back with Live within about a second, on the drum pads or the keyboard. To switch between the two on the fly, use v1.6.1 (in the same download) in NI's MIDI mode, where SHIFT + MASCHINE (MK3, MASCHINE+: SHIFT + CHANNEL) switches between MASCHINE and Live. Or play the Expansions' kits without the plug-in: BROWSER > MASCHINE Kits (see BROWSER: browse and load). On Windows you can also keep the plug-in in the set and the controller with Live (see MASCHINE VSTi in Live Set Support).

notes.title: Activate once on each computer
notes.text: Until this computer is activated, the controller shows the activation pages and Live doesn't connect. Press the encoder: the activation page opens in your browser. Your browser may ask whether this page may talk to apps on this computer: choose Allow. That lets the page reach MASCHINE for Ableton Live on this computer, and nothing else. Enter the licence key from your purchase email and the email you bought with, then Activate. Within a few seconds the controller works and Live connects. There are two editions. MIKRO MK3 covers the MIKRO MK3. MK3, MASCHINE+ & MIKRO MK3 covers all three controllers. A key works on 3 computers. Moving to another one? Open the same page and choose Deactivate this computer first. Once activated, it works offline too. It checks itself online now and then, and a computer that stays offline for 90 days is asked to go online once.

sections.title: PATTERN: clips
sections.summary: A 4x4 view of Live's Session clips (4 tracks x 4 scenes). Pad colours follow the clip colours; playing clips are bright, and a clip waiting to start (Live's launch quantization) blinks in its colour, red when it will record. Recording a new clip (an empty slot, or VARIATION + pad) selects its track, so Live's auto-arm arms it (the dimmed arm, which follows the track you select; tracks armed for real are disarmed), and the pads switch to the drum pads or the keyboard so you can play into it right away. With a Record length set (REC + TURN), the new clip records exactly that many bars and then loops.

sections.title: PAD MODE: drums
sections.summary: The 16 visible pads of the track's Drum Rack. Hitting a pad plays it and focuses it in Live (like MASCHINE focusing a sound). Pads are coloured by chain colour or by name (see the colour table); a muted pad (or one silenced by another's solo) is dim white, a step brighter when selected, as in TRACK. While a clip plays, the pads of the notes it plays light up. Hold a pad and turn for a quick edit, as in MASCHINE: TURN changes its volume (1 dB a click, SHIFT + TURN 0.1 dB), PUSH + TURN its tune in semitones (its Simpler or Drum Sampler). The pad still plays; the screen shows the pad and the value until you let go. Hold several pads to change them together, each from its own level; one hold is one undo step.
sections.swatches_note: Name colours: pads use their chain colour by default; press PAD MODE again to colour them by name instead (it is remembered). A chain without a colour also gets its name colour. The name is read word by word, first word first, as sample names start with the kind of sound (Kick BlackEarth 1, ClosedHH Dev, BD_Deep_01); a word counts when it starts with one of these words, and short abbreviations (BD, SN, HH, OH ...) only as whole words. Anything else is white.

Root and scale are Live's own, so changing them here changes Live's Scale settings and vice versa, including per-clip scales. While a clip plays, the pads of the notes it plays light up. The pads are in the track's colour (with a MIDI clip selected: the clip's) and follow it at once when you recolour it. On a track with a Drum Rack, KEYBOARD gives the drum pads.

sections.title: STEP: step sequencer
sections.summary: The pads are 16 steps of the focused sound (the focused drum pad, or the last keyboard note) in the focused clip, read like text as in MASCHINE: step 1 top left (pad 13), step 16 bottom right (pad 4). The playhead runs across the pads while the clip plays, and the page follows it on longer clips (after you change the page yourself, it follows again once the playhead reaches your page). Hold a step to edit it, as in MASCHINE: the screen shows Step N and its value; TURN changes the velocity (1-127), SHIFT + TURN the length in steps, PUSH + TURN nudges the note up to 7/16 of a step earlier or later. Hold several steps to change them together; one hold is one undo step. A tap on a lit step removes it when you let go. On a Drum Rack the steps light in the selected drum pad's colour and follow when you pick another pad; on an instrument track, in the clip's colour.

notes.title: Held buttons and combos
notes.text: Hold ERASE, DUPLICATE, EVENTS, SOLO, MUTE or SELECT and press another button: that is a combo. Letting go of the held button then does nothing, so a combo never ends in an extra tap. SHIFT and STOP are not affected.

sections.title: MASCHINE VSTi in Live Set Support (Windows)
sections.summary: Keep NI's MASCHINE plug-in in your Live sets, and your controller stays with Live. You switch it on from the controller: NI VSTi support, on the settings page. It is off by default. Off is how NI's software works today: the MASCHINE plug-in takes the controller as soon as it is in the set (see Getting started). On: while Live runs, NI's background helper is paused. So the MASCHINE plug-in can't take the controller. It stays with MASCHINE for Ableton Live. When Live closes, the helper starts again by itself. That also happens after a crash. Windows only for now. macOS is coming.

tour.intro: Keep the MASCHINE plug-in in your Live sets, and your controller stays with Live. Windows, switched on from the controller.

notes.title: Switch it on or off
notes.text: Live can stay open. On the MK3 press SETTINGS and open the Setup tab. On the MIKRO press MASCHINE and turn to NI VSTi support, just before About. Turn its knob (MIKRO: press ◀ or ▶). A dialog explains what it does, with CANCEL highlighted. Choose CONFIRM, and Windows asks for your permission once. The value shows the new state at once. That lets your Windows user pause and restart one NI helper, NI Host Integration Agent. Nothing else changes: no other service, no driver and no NI setting. To switch it off, do the same again. MASCHINE Setup (in the download, choice 2, with Live closed) still does the same, if you ever need it.

notes.title: MK3 screens and NI VSTi support
notes.text: Switch the MK3 screens back to MASCHINE while NI VSTi support is on, and the screens go black: NI's helper is paused while Live runs. When Live closes, MASCHINE and Komplete Kontrol show the screens again.

notes.title: What you give up while Live runs
notes.text: You can't control the MASCHINE plug-in from the controller. Its browser and its pages are mouse only. This comes back when Live closes.

sections.title: Mixer: VOLUME tap
sections.summary: A VOLUME tap turns the controller into a mixer. The pads show your tracks as in TRACK mode, each in its colour and glowing with its level (muted tracks dim white); the visited track's pad is white. The screen shows that track and its parameter, with a fill bar along the bottom; the encoder and the touch strip change it. Visiting a track doesn't select it in Live: you can mix one track while playing another. MUTE, SOLO and SELECT light for the visited track, and their taps act on it. Values land exactly on Live's 0.1 dB steps.

sections.title: PLUG-IN: device parameters (MIKRO)
sections.summary: The encoder controls one parameter of the selected device at a time. Parameters come in pages: Ableton's own banks for Live's devices (Filter, Envelope...), the visible macros of a rack, or groups of 8 for plug-ins. The screen shows the device, the page and how many there are (Macros 2/2; on two lines, the device after the track's box on line 1 and the count in the corner), and the parameter's name and value. A rack has as many macros as it shows in Live (click the rack's + macro button for up to 16); a hidden macro you renamed or mapped stays reachable on a last page, and showing or hiding macros updates the pages at once. Each device remembers where you were.

notes.title: Simpler
notes.text: On a Simpler the first page (Main) starts with Mode: Classic, One-Shot or Slicing (turning it switches Simpler's mode in Live). Next comes Filter Freq, or in Slicing Cursor: a position in the sample, shown as a time; PUSH on it adds a slice marker there, or removes the slice marker the cursor is on. When the cursor sits on a slice marker, its time ends with the marker's number (for example 1.00 s #4), so you know which marker PUSH removes. Then S Start and S Length in Classic. In One-Shot and Slicing they are Start and End, which move the sample's start and end markers (the ones you drag with the mouse). Filter Res (in Slicing also Filter Freq) comes first on the Filter page. Tip: with SNAP on in Simpler, Start and Length jump in big steps (Live snaps them to the sample's transients, with the mouse too). Turn SNAP off in Simpler to move them freely.

sections.title: BROWSER: browse and load (MIKRO)
sections.summary: Live's browser on the hardware screen, Favorites first (what you starred with SHIFT + STAR, and the kits you starred in MASCHINE), then Live's sidebar: Collections (Live's Favorites and your coloured collections), MASCHINE Kits, Live Sets, the library (Sounds, Drums, Instruments ...), and the folders you added to Places. Live Sets opens at once and lists the sets in your User Library, your Places and the current project, newest first; PUSH on one opens it at once, as a double click on the file would (Live asks to save your changes first, as usual). MASCHINE Kits (with MASCHINE Expansions or the MASCHINE library installed; any Live 12) lists your Expansions and their kits: PUSH on a kit loads it as a Drum Rack, pad for pad as in MASCHINE: onto the selected MIDI track, replacing its instrument (effects after it stay), or on a new MIDI track named after the kit (# Kit name, so Live numbers it) when an audio track is selected. Each pad is a Simpler in 1-Shot, so a hit rings out; long synth, vocal, FX, atmosphere and loop sounds play while held instead. The pads and the Drum Rack's chains get the drum colours by sound name (see PAD MODE). A drum-synth sound plays NI's recording of it where there is one; a sound that is a plug-in in MASCHINE (Massive, Monark ...) stays an empty pad with its name, to put your own sound on. Turning onto a kit plays NI's own preview of it through Live's preview (Cue output, preview switched on in Live's browser), like clicking a sample in Live's browser; the script puts the previews in your User Library (MASCHINE Kit Previews, as hard links: no extra disk space) the first time you open MASCHINE Kits, and picks up newly installed Expansions the same way. On Live 12.0 to 12.3 the kits are prepared once, in the background, the first time MASCHINE Kits opens: they are listed at once, with a Preparing kits 42% row on top that counts up and goes by itself (after a Live restart it carries on where it stopped). A kit you push before it is ready is prepared first and loads by itself in a moment. You'll also see the kits in Live's browser, under User Library > MASCHINE Kit Presets. Your MASCHINE favourites come along, in a one-way sync: the kits you star in MASCHINE show with a ★ in Favorites and in MASCHINE Kits' own Favorites folder, next to the ones you starred on the controller (a kit starred in both is listed once). Star or unstar kits in MASCHINE and the lists follow, also while Live runs (the next time the list opens). The controller only reads MASCHINE's favourites and never changes them: a kit starred in MASCHINE stays starred here (the screen says Still starred / in MASCHINE; star / unstar it in MASCHINE). Expansions you add or remove are followed: a removed Expansion's kits leave the lists, and a new one's favourites appear once MASCHINE has scanned it. Favorites lists are sorted by name, as in MASCHINE. This is the way to play the Expansions in Live without the MASCHINE plug-in, which takes the controller away from the script (see Getting started).

sections.title: MASCHINE: settings (MIKRO)
sections.summary: Your preferences, on the controller. They are saved with Live's preferences on your computer, remembered after a restart, and take effect at once (Start mode: at the next start). The screen saver only darkens the screen: the pad and button lights stay as they are, and the press, pad hit, turn or strip touch that wakes it still does its job (a pad plays). It never darkens the waiting and setup screens. Record length is the same setting as hold REC + TURN (see Transport). Start mode Pads opens on the drum pads on a track with a Drum Rack, else on the keyboard; the start mode also applies when the controller comes back from the MASCHINE plug-in. On Windows the list ends with NI VSTi support (see MASCHINE VSTi in Live Set Support), then About. A switch like that asks first, in the popup: CANCEL or CONFIRM, the highlighted one in brackets, CANCEL first. Turn to move, PUSH to choose.

changes.v1: NI's MIDI mode: SHIFT + MASCHINE (MK3, MASCHINE+: SHIFT + CHANNEL) switches between MASCHINE and the script
changes.v2: The script steps aside while a MASCHINE plug-in is in the set and comes back when it is deleted (or use v1.6.1 to switch on the fly). Windows: with NI VSTi support on (on the controller), the plug-in stays in the set and the controller stays with Live
MASCHINE's pages for Live on both screens (mixer, devices as pictures, browser, Section page ...). Switched on from the controller: SETTINGS twice, no restart, on macOS and Windows
On the controller: MIKRO MASCHINE (a list), MK3 SETTINGS (four tabs on the knobs). A switch that changes something outside Live asks first: CANCEL or CONFIRM
